To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a collagen patch loaded with autologous MSCs is a promising strategy for the treatment of chronic MI.

the epicardial implantation of a collagen scaffold seeded with autologous bone marrow-derived mesenchymal cells (MSCs), in a rat model of chronic MI, contributes to the improvement of cardiac function and remodeling.
the 3D collagen scaffold promotes the survival of the autologous mesengenic cells, the epicardial patch improves the cardiac perfusion and limits the ventricular remodeling in chronic MI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new strategy to repair the chronic myocardial infersction.
the development of an innovative approach to the treatment of chronic MI, using autologous MSCs seeded onto a collagen matrix.
the use of autologous MSCs seeded on collagen- 1 scaffold for the repair of myocardial infarct.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3D-MSC-patch engrafts the MI and contributes to reverse remodeling.
this study provides a proof of concept for the feasibility and safety of MSCs-collagen patch in the treatment of chronic MI.
3D-collagene MSC patch is a promising strategy for myocardial repair.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MSCs are able to repair the heart after myocardial infarctions.
MSCs are a promising candidate for cardiac regeneration.
MSC-collagen patches are effective in repairing chronic MI and in reducing ventricular remodeling in rat.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 3D collagen scaffold is able to maintain the phenotype and potentiality of MSCs and that MSCs can be engineered to repair chronic MI.
a collagen scaffold can be engineered to support the engraftment of MSCs and promote their differentiation to myofibroblasts and angiogenesis.
the use of MSCs on a collagen matrix can be an effective strategy to treat chronic myocardial infersction.
